chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Permission from his sister; tutors Cook and Latimore
summary: His sister agreed provided he had tutors, so Cook and the lawyer-manager George W. Latimore became his guardians; Cricket Smith congratulated him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I said, "Well, I'll have to see my older sister and find out whether she will permit me to."
Well, you were how old at this time, eighteen?
Sixteen. No, seventeen -- seventeen? Eighteen? No, no, seventeen.
Seventeen.
She said, yes, and so I spoke to my sister and asked her to speak to Mr. Spooner, and going back to Mr. Marshall, Glaudius Marshall, who was the first person I had, wonderful man.
He said, "Well, if there's a chance to -- why, not, Marion Cook is a man that's known, universally known, and known more in the United States as a very, very good musician."
I have quite a lot of things about his pedigree, you know.
Right.
Briggs
And he uh -- she said, 'You take a chance, but that will have to be a tutor, because you're not of age.' So both of them, Latimore, and Dad Cook became my tutors.
Latimore was who, now?
He was a business manager.
What was his first name?
George W. Latimore. George W. --
Latimore. He was black as well?
Yes, he was black. And he was a lawyer. He was a lawyer.
I see.
And he was a businessman and lawyer, and his brother was a broker.
I see.
Briggs
That was funny, in those days there were only two, no others. There were two colored brokers on Wall Street. Just he and his brother.
And that was it?

Yes. And he and Lattimore was the sponsor. He was a business manager and a sponsor and everything. And they were taking the orchestra out, after rehearsal -- about Cricket Smith, he was sick, he couldn't make it.
So, Cricket came back and when he came back he grabbed me and kissed me and he said, 'Son, I hope this will be a stepping stone in life for you, you know.' Well, he said, 'I'm so glad for you.'
We went on tour --
